messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Pcountopen detection models problems
parts:
Don,

You can't have missing covariate values for any observations, even ones that did not occur.  And this isn't unique to unmarked, this is a basic linear modeling requirement.  In your case, unmarked is throwing out a site or row any time it has an NA under an observation-level covariate.  Since some (or many) of your sites have at least 1 NA for a given observation, the entire site gets dropped.

One solution is to impute values for the missing covariates that correspond to the mean for actual observations.  There is discussion of this elsewhere on the Google group, and on the internet in general (e.g., StackOverflow), because it is not a perfect solution for a number of reasons.

obs.covs$time[is.na(obs.covs$time)] <- 0   #given standardized covariates

But I think it can generally work well here since the missing covariates are affecting the observation/detection process and not the state process.  For instance, if you had missing site-level covariates, that might be more problematic.  I'm curious what others think about that though.

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Pcountopen detection models problems
parts:
Dan, if there are NAs in an observation-level covariate, unmarked only discards the corresponding values in the response variable. It doesn't discard the entire site. 

Don, you have 3 missing values in your observation-level covariates that correspond to observed data in the response variable. The following code replace the 3 values of y with NAs. Now it runs without a warning message.


sum(is.na(obs.cov$time) & !is.na(y))
sum(is.na(obs.cov$date) & !is.na(y))

which(is.na(obs.cov$time) & !is.na(y))
which(is.na(obs.cov$date) & !is.na(y))

y[is.na(obs.cov$time)] <- NA
y[is.na(obs.cov$date)] <- NA


beviumf<- unmarkedFramePCO(y=y, obsCovs=obs.cov, siteCovs=site.cov, yearlySiteCovs=yearly.site.covs, numPrimary=T)

#Best Fit Detection Models
BEVI<-list()

BEVI$nulldatetime<-pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~1,~date+time, beviumf, mixture="P",dynamics="constant", K=50)
BEVI$nulldate<-pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~1, ~date, beviumf, mixture="P",dynamics="constant", K=50)
BEVI$nulltime<-pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~1, ~time, beviumf, mixture="P",dynamics="constant", K=50)
BEVI$null<-pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~1,~1, beviumf, mixture="P",dynamics="constant", K=50)
